Data concerning the occurrence of surface water in the Project Area are limited and include only information that has been collected since the latter part of 1972 by Westmoreland Resources. The U.S. Geological survey began monitoring flow in Sarpy Creek near its mouth in September, 1973, and on Tullock Creek near its mouth in September, 1974. During March, 1975, Westmoreland Resources began collecting more detailed surface-water data at seven sites on or near the leased area. These sites included two on Sarpy Creek, two on East Fork Sarpy Creek, and one each on Middle Fork Sarpy Creek, Pleasant Creek, and Plum Creek, respectively. Locations of these sites and available stream flow data are given in Appendix D: Although no long-term surface water data have been collected in the Project Area, several larger streams in the vicinity have been monitored for many years. Gaging stations include those on the Bighorn, Little Bighorn, Tongue and Yellowstone Rivers in Montana and Wyoming. Average annual runoff per unit area contributing to stream flow is 0.25 inches or about 13 acre-feet per square mile (U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, 1972, U.S. Geological Survey and Montana Bureau of Mines, 1963, U.S. Bureau of Indian Affairs, 1974).
Base-line studies during the period from March through November, 1975, indicate that surface-water flow in most drainages located within the Project Area ceases by midsummer. However, flow was observed at three locations subsequent to that time including East Fork Sarpy Creek at Site 4, Pleasant Creek at Site 5, and on Middle Fork Sarpy Creek at Site 7.
